primary_claim: A prototype LLM 'debugger' using SAE features and a new ablation technique ('cluster resampling') automates interpretable circuit visualization for arbitrary prompts on a small character-level toy GPT-2 model, producing smaller/sparser circuits (e.g. 20-41 features) than conventional zero-ablation (31-138 features) or resample-ablation (70-96 features) at a comparable or better KL divergence target.

effect.metric: number of SAE features per extracted circuit at KL divergence threshold 0.25
effect.value: cluster resampling circuits contain fewer features (e.g. 20-41 across example sequences) than zero ablation (31-138) and conventional resampling (70-96)

contradicts_or_qualifies: addresses the common criticism that mechanistic interpretability has yet to deliver approaches that clearly outperform baseline techniques, by showing cluster resampling outperforms zero- and resample-ablation baselines on their toy model
stated_future_work: scale to models with around a billion parameters (e.g. DeepSeek R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, Apple OpenELM), reattempting analysis on similar architectures at larger configurations
SAE training techniques that build on features extracted from upstream layers, e.g. crosscoders
speed up or approximate cluster resampling for production-scale models, e.g. via efficient k-nearest neighbor search or ideas from attribution patching
investigate the phenomenon where ablating certain individual latents brings model outputs closer to the original output than when all latents are present
train SAE features on highly targeted datasets (e.g. mathematical material) to study chain-of-thought reasoning related to math capabilities
limitations_stated: the model analyzed is very small, and current limitations in SAE training techniques suggest there may be constraints on the model sizes that can be effectively studied
cluster resampling is slow because it requires a mean squared error calculation over cached values representing the entire training dataset
with conventional resampling, they were unable to achieve the target KL divergence of 0.25
the positional-dimension clustering trick is not expected to be useful for modern architectures, most of which use rotational position embeddings instead of absolute ones
quote: Cluster resampling produces the best results, followed by zero ablation, then distantly by conventional resampling.
